# Optimization Methods

Master's *Optimization Methods* course at Wrocław University of Science and Technology (FICT,
lectures by M. Przewoźniczek). **Three self-contained deliverables under one guided-tour README** —
see [[readme-as-guided-tour]], of which this repo is the strongest instance in the corpus.

| # | Unit | What it is | Stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `first_project/` | {{permutation-flow-shop-scheduling}} benchmark — five methods raced on six Taillard instances | C++17 (std-only) + [[cmake]] + Python plotting |
| 2 | `final_project/` | [[multi-depot-vehicle-routing]] on real OpenStreetMap road networks, with a 32-combination {{operator-bake-off}} and a submitted 32-page paper | C++17 (std-only) + [[osmnx]] / [[networkx]] / [[matplotlib]] + [[leaflet]] |
| 3 | `exam_prep/` | 24-chapter interactive study guide, 23 canvas demos, zero dependencies | Vanilla ES6 + HTML5 Canvas |

335 files / ~8.2 MB readable text. 102 PNG, 30 CSV, 19 `.cpp`, 12 `.h`, 10 `.hpp`, 17 `.js`, 17 `.md`,
2 PDF (one 11 MB). Remote over SSH, branch `main` with `master` merged in.

## The git history splits the corpus's strongest pattern

This is the headline finding of the ingest. 69 commits over **105 days** through 2026-07-10 — the
whole coursework history, and the 70th commit is the 2026-08-01 repair above — author date ==
commit date throughout, **seven distinct working dates**, four `Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/master'`
commits proving work across two machines, a structural refactor (`b66a594 changed folder structure`,
78 renames), and a real mid-stream bug fix:

> Optimization Methods, git commit d72e8bf "fixed no run on tabu search on high talliard instances",
> 2026-04-07

That commit adds `std::max(1, totalBudget/neighbourhoodSize)` — on `tai500_20_0` the integer division
floored the budget to **zero**, so Tabu Search never iterated. A bug found by running the thing, fixed
in place, committed the day it was found. `tabuSize parameter was added` follows three minutes later.

**But the repo is not uniform.** 44 of 69 commits land on one day (2026-04-20), 17 of them a
mechanical one-file-per-commit comment sweep. Then an **81-day silence**, after which
`final_project` arrives as **one commit of 224 files / 17,075 insertions** and `exam_prep` as **one
commit of 5 files / 4,608 insertions**. Internal timestamps prove the work predates the commits by
months — `DATA_VERIFICATION.md` says "Date of check: 2026-07-09", `comparison_detailed.txt` is
described as generated 2026-06-16.

**Verdict: `first_project` is a genuine working log; `final_project` and `exam_prep` are a publishing
dump.** Recorded on [[import-finished-work-into-git]] as its one split case. The last four commits are
pure presentation — linguist marking, tech-stack section, MIT licence, licence badges — i.e.
[[presentation-polish-tail-commits]].

## Verification is auditing, not testing

**There are no unit tests anywhere in either project.** Verification is entirely post-hoc artefact
auditing, and unusually good at it: `tools/verify_reports.py` re-parses all 36 solver reports
(trip-distance sums to ±1 m, demand == load, load ≤ capacity, every customer served exactly once)
**and cross-checks a hard-coded copy of the paper's Table 7 to ±2 m** — a real external check, not a
self-check. `verify_chromosomes.py` checks 12 chromosomes are valid permutations with in-range,
**non-monotonic** depot genes. `docs/DATA_VERIFICATION.md` is dated, and the result is surfaced as a
README badge (`data checks 36/36 ✓`) with re-run instructions. See [[generated-audit-artifact]].

The repo also states what it could **not** verify, in the shipped prose rather than a footnote —
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]. It advertises its own negative results: the GA losing to
greedy ([[blind-baseline-comparison]]) and a parameter change that backfired
([[revert-depot-mutation-rate-raise]]).

## Findings

- **`CMakeLists.txt` line 1 was `cmake_minimum_required(3.16)` — the `VERSION` keyword missing**, so
  the README's "recommended" CMake path could not configure, and the committed prebuilt `pfsp.exe`
  was the real run path. **Fixed 2026-08-01** in `d116a84`, which also gave `project(PFSP CXX)` its
  language; the file now reads `cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)`. The finding stands as a
  finding — it was true for the whole life of the coursework — and is retired as a live defect.
  Details and the full reasoning on [[cmake]]. `confidence: high`, both states read directly.
- **A negative reproducibility result, kept.** Re-running the deterministic `greedy` on a freshly
  downloaded Wrocław graph gave 178,207 / 322,318 / 458,921 m against the paper's 177,555 / 299,944 /
  481,089 m — OSM has drifted. Recorded on [[osmnx]] and [[multi-depot-vehicle-routing]].
- **[[documentation-drift]], four instances.** `first_project/README.md` still says "No license file
  is currently included in this repository" three months after MIT was added at root;
  `mdvrp/README.md` says "never new executables" while `ARCHITECTURE.md` §7 lists six;
  `HOW_TO_RUN.md` names two scripts that do not exist — **self-flagged in the audit rather than
  fixed**; `exam_prep/README.md` says 24 chapters while `chapters.js` says "Twenty-five chapters".
- **The `.gitattributes` is about language stats, not binaries.** Two `linguist-generated=true` rules
  only, so GitHub stops labelling the repo "100% JavaScript" when most of those bytes are generated
  map-coordinate data. No Git LFS; the 11 MB PDF and `pfsp.exe` are committed raw.
- No `.claude/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/` or `.vscode/` anywhere — this repo contradicts
  [[agent-skills-checked-into-the-repo]].
- `final_project/docs/` uses SHOUTY topic filenames with no numeric prefixes; numbering lives inside
  content (chapters 01–24, `ARCHITECTURE.md` §1–§10, combos C01–C32). Contradicts
  [[numbered-docs-chapters]] and [[numbered-stages-in-directory-names]].
